clue.text: Deceives girl about heavy metal

indicators.note: the girl's title is wrapped about the metal, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: Miss is the title of a girl or unmarried woman
lead is a notably heavy metallic element

explanation.surface: A girl tells lies about heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' looks like the music genre, but here it is simply the dense element.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone is to give them a false impression, which is to deceive them.

clue.text: Cheese with fine Greek character?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheese of excellent Greek personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests personality but means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white brined cheese, an example of the category.

clue.text: Spanish destroyer as escort at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Spanish warship serves as a naval escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' suggests a warship, but it is the conquistador who destroyed the Aztec empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hernan Cortes was the Spanish conquistador whose campaign brought down the Aztec empire.

clue.text: Make investment, for example, that's easily shifted around

indicators.note: letters that are shifted around are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice that an investment is one easily moved about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial, but to invest a town is to surround it with troops, an old military sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Investment in the military sense is besieging, so to make one is to begin a blockade of a town.

clue.text: Is a bit less wobbly

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the preceding words are set shaking into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is becoming a little steadier.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'wobbly' shakes up IS A BIT LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that steadies itself becomes firmer and less prone to shaking.

clue.text: American's lines — pronounced as signals for actors

indicators.note: pronounced as says the next word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: cues are the prompts telling actors when to speak or enter

explanation.surface: An American's lines spoken as prompts for performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests a script, which the actors reinforce, but it is what Americans call a waiting line.
explanation.definitionFit: Where the British say queue, Americans say line, so these are what an American would call lines.

clue.text: Minor way lawyer or editor is suffering reverse

indicators.note: suffering reverse means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer or editor suffers a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering reverse' reads as a setback, but it turns the whole string DA OR ED IS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A side road is a minor road branching off a main one.

clue.text: Raised bar established for county

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is written upwards

parts.note: a rod is a straight bar
set means fixed or established

explanation.surface: A bar was raised to set up a county.
explanation.walkthrough: DORSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is an English county on the south coast.

clue.text: A part that's absorbing to perform in theatre

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a cut is a share or portion

explanation.surface: An engrossing role to play on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbing' reads as gripping, but it is the container signal; 'part' means a share, not a stage role.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a scene is to perform it, playing it as drama.

clue.text: Russian female collegian ignoring the odds

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A Russian student defies the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring the odds' sounds like defying chances, but it discards the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a common Russian woman's first name.

clue.text: After short time, vessel's sailor, exhausted, changes direction

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an urn is a vessel; with the 's it gives a plural-looking piece
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
out means used up or finished

explanation.surface: After a short spell, the ship's tired sailor changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a pot, an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn about is to reverse one's heading, which is changing direction.

clue.text: Article in newspaper introducing old copper baths

indicators.note: in places the article inside the newspaper

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a is the indefinite article
the as was an old Roman coin made of copper

explanation.surface: A newspaper article launches old police officers into the baths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but the as was an ancient Roman copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Saunas are steam baths, an example of the wider sense of bath.

clue.text: Where oil may be applied for close shave

definitions.meaning: read literally, oil goes near a squeak, where a hinge is creaking

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the phrase literally; the second is its idiomatic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A near squeak is an informal phrase for a narrow escape, just like a close shave.

clue.text: Spectacle?

parts.note: spectacles come as a pair of lenses; a single one, a monocle, would be a lone spectacle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacle' looks like a show, but the question mark hints at one half of a pair of spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A single lens worn to aid sight, a monocle, is in effect one spectacle.

clue.text: Used brand available in main primary colour

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
red is one of the primary colours

explanation.surface: A second-hand brand of paint sold in a strong red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is a poetic word for the ocean; 'Used brand' means applied a branding iron.
explanation.definitionFit: To brand is to burn a mark with hot iron, and seared means scorched in exactly that way.

clue.text: A detente arranged, of the type that lacks teeth

definitions.text: of the type that lacks teeth

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detente is set up between parties without teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: A toothless detente is a nice image, but 'arranged' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate means without teeth, and names mammals such as anteaters lacking front teeth.

clue.text: Studied coral initially, say, in waters off Africa

indicators.note: say tells us the pieces are spoken, so their sound is entered

parts.note: studied is READ in its past tense, pronounced red, and coral initially is its first letter C, which sounds like sea

explanation.surface: Someone studied coral, for example, in African waters.
explanation.walkthrough: READ in the past tense sounds like RED, and the letter C sounds like SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea lies between north-east Africa and Arabia.

clue.text: Snake possible to find in wild parts of Canada

indicators.note: in puts the feasible piece inside the jumbled letters
wild suggests disorder, so the parts of the word are scrambled

parts.note: on means feasible, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: A snake might be found in the wilder regions of Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild parts of' signals an anagram of the country's name; anacondas do not live in Canada, hence 'possible'.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a very large South American constrictor snake.

clue.text: Bothersome child, source of trouble and wrongdoing

indicators.note: source of picks out the beginning, the first letter of trouble

parts.note: an error is a mistake or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A pesky child brings trouble and mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: A terror is an informal name for a naughty child, a holy terror.

clue.text: Modern composer I heard on artificial organ

parts.note: Philip Glass is a modern American composer

indicators.note: heard means the word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE

explanation.surface: A modern composer plays on a synthetic organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument, which the composer reinforces, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass eye is a prosthetic replacing a lost eye, which is an organ of sight.

clue.text: Working party

definitions.meaning: the British ... Party, a major UK political party

explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of the main UK political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour means work or toil, and is also the name of a British political party.

clue.text: Islander's capital taken in main assault

indicators.note: taken in says the letters are concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An island capital is captured in a major assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital of the Bahamas sits inside 'main assault'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas, an island nation.

clue.text: Senior citizen supporting refusals? Impossible!

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting below the other piece

parts.note: noes are refusals
OAP is old-age pensioner, British for a senior citizen

explanation.surface: A pensioner props up a series of refusals and exclaims it can't be done.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is British shorthand for old-age pensioner; 'no soap' is slang for no chance.
explanation.definitionFit: No soap is an idiom meaning it cannot be done, a flat refusal.

clue.text: Changes of mind that could get bats run out

indicators.note: could get suggests the letters of the following words might be turned into something new

explanation.surface: Turnarounds in a cricket match where batsmen are run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats run out' looks like cricket, but its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn is a reversal of opinion, a complete change of mind.

clue.text: Miss love inside here?

indicators.note: inside places the zero within the young woman

parts.note: a gal is a girl, a Miss
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Somewhere you would pine for love while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue is definition and wordplay: a prison is where one misses love.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaol, a prison, is where inmates are locked away from loved ones.

clue.text: Good wood to cut

parts.note: ash is a kind of timber

explanation.surface: Good timber to be sawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a deep cut or wound.

clue.text: Excel in relation to roles where French diplomacy succeeds

indicators.note: succeeds means comes after, so the diplomacy follows the French word

parts.note: ou is French for where
tact is diplomatic skill

explanation.surface: Excelling in roles where French diplomacy works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeds' looks like doing well but means follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To outact someone is to outperform them in acting parts.

clue.text: Critical attack without leader in place, by the way

indicators.note: without leader removes the first letter

parts.note: a broadside is a fierce verbal attack

explanation.surface: A critical attack lacking a leader, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like an aside but means beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside is the strip of ground at the edge of a road, the spot by the way.
